name: Deep Gull Grey
lede: Deep Gull Grey is a mid, barely green grey named for the seabird, recorded by Ridgway in 1912, carried into the ISCC-NBS system of 1955, and also an approximate match for a RAL paint color.

sections.title: Named for the gull
sections.body:
Our data traces the name to the gull, the seabird, a plant-and-landscape word rather than a pigment [1]. Ridgway's 1912 atlas plots it on plate LIII at hue 75, tone -7, read from an aged scan, and the same area was carried into the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 as block 265 [1]. The paint standard RAL also lists an approximate match, RAL 9007, under a different name [1]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 59, chroma 3, hue 144 degrees: a mid-value, almost unsaturated grey [1].

Its nearest distinct neighbor by computed color distance is [[greenish-grey|Greenish Grey]], 2.6 units away and read in our data as "almost the same" [2]. The RAL match, Grey Aluminium, sits even closer at 2.3 units, also a near-duplicate [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a close match covers enough of the canvas in 386, as photographed, more common than 80 percent of the named colors we track [4]. It peaks in paintings from the 1900s, at 1.8 times the rate expected from that century's share of the archive [4]. Eugène Boudin is its most devoted painter here, with the color present in 6 of 33 of his works, nearly seven times the baseline of the museums those works come from [4]. It shares canvases more than chance with [[dim-grey|Dim Grey]] and [[agate-grey|Agate Grey]], two other quiet greys [4].
